To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel approach to learning deformable point set registration by incorporating learned regularized feature descriptors into the coherent point drift algorithm, which is evaluated for the challenging problem of aligning keypoints of lung CT scans in COPD patients.
We present a new method for learning regularized feature descriptors for point sets with dynamic graph CNN.

the proposed method is able to: 1) learn geometric features from point sets, 2) incorporate these features into a registration method and 3) outperforms the state-of-the-art on lung registration in COPD patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether it is possible to learn geometrically meaningful descriptors of point sets with deep networks.
the question, how to learn regularized feature descriptors on irregular domains and how these can be incorporated in a registration pipeline.
learning regularized feature descriptors on irregular domains and the integration into a deformable point registration framework.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed method outperforms all other methods in all metrics, which is not only a significant improvement over the state-of-the-art in lung registration but also a promising step forward for learning based point set registration in general.
our approach outperforms the baseline methods by 10.5% in terms of mean absolute landmark distance (MALD) and 7.8% in terms of Dice score (DS) in a challenging lung registration task.
the proposed method is able to establish descriptive point descriptors, which can be used as prior knowledge to significantly improve the registration of lung keypoints in patients with severe COPD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the recently developed dynamic graph CNNs can be used to learn regularized feature descriptors, and we have shown that these learned features can be successfully used to improve the performance of a deformable registration framework.
the combination of dynamic graph CNNs and CPD is a powerful and promising framework for learning deformable registration.

the geometric deep learning framework allows us to learn regularized features from irregular data, which can be incorporated into existing registration methods to yield an end to end learning approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
geometric deep learning is not only applicable for dense voxel data but also for sparse and irregular data, e.g. keypoints, which can be of great value for the analysis of medical point set data.

geometric deep learning can be used to learn powerful regularized features from irregular domains, which can be incorporated into existing registration algorithms to improve robustness and performance.
deep learning methods can be successfully applied to deformable registration of point sets.
